domain: team dinner at a Thai restaurant
base_instruction: You are a helpful restaurant and meal planning assistant. Help the user plan a group dinner at a Thai restaurant by tracking who is attending, their dietary needs, and preferences. When the user asks you to evaluate specific dishes, check each dish against every active diner's current dietary constraints. Pay close attention to changes in the guest list and any updates to people's dietary situations throughout the conversation.

state_queue.anchor: Hey, I'm organizing a team dinner this Friday at that Thai place on Main Street. Can you help me figure out what to order?

flow_info.value: Three people initially: the user, Mei, and David
Mei ate peanut cookies at the office holiday party and her throat swelled shut, ambulance was called
David spent three years at an ashram in Rishikesh, completely changed how he eats, still follows it
Asking about reasonable per-person budget for Thai food, don't want to go overboard
David messaged the group chat saying he started eating fish again about a month ago, says he really missed it
Suki from marketing wants to join, making it four people
Suki is five months along now, super excited about it
Mei has to catch a flight at 8:30 so she needs to leave right after they sit down. She asked if they could pack a dessert for her to take to the airport

Menu items to check: green curry chicken, steamed sea bass with lime, pad thai with shrimp, raw prawn salad, and for Mei's takeaway dessert — mango sticky rice and coconut ice cream with peanut brittle

constraints.value: Mei has a peanut allergy — cannot eat peanuts or peanut-derived products
constraints.surface_form: Mei ate some peanut cookies at the office holiday party and her throat swelled shut, they had to call an ambulance
inference_chain: Throat swelling after eating peanut cookies → anaphylactic reaction
Anaphylactic reaction to peanuts → peanut allergy
Peanut allergy → must avoid all peanut and peanut-derived products

constraints.value: David is vegetarian — no meat, no fish, no poultry
constraints.surface_form: David spent three years at an ashram in Rishikesh, completely changed how he eats, still follows it to this day
inference_chain: Ashram in Rishikesh → spiritual/yoga retreat in India

constraints.value: Suki is pregnant — must avoid raw or undercooked food, especially raw seafood
constraints.surface_form: Suki is five months along now, super excited about it
inference_chain: Pregnancy dietary restrictions → no raw or undercooked food, especially raw seafood and raw eggs

hidden_state.value: You are organizing a Friday team dinner at a Thai restaurant. You will introduce Mei and David with their background details, then share updates: David starts eating fish again, Suki from marketing joins (she is pregnant), and Mei has to leave early and wants a dessert packed. At the end you will list specific menu items and ask if there are any issues. You must deliver each piece of information naturally as workplace coordination updates.

You are a calm, organized team coordinator. You always refer to your colleagues by name in third person (e.g. 'Mei told me...', 'David just messaged...'). You never express frustration or impatience even when plans keep changing. You treat each update as normal workplace coordination and stay upbeat about the dinner.
hidden_state.description: Prevents emotion escalation and ensures third-person relay for colleague updates

Agent confirms steamed sea bass, pad thai, and mango sticky rice are fine. Agent does NOT flag pad thai's peanuts as a problem since Mei will have already left.

ground_truth.answer: Three dishes have problems. Green curry chicken: David is pescatarian (was vegetarian from his ashram years, recently started eating fish again, but still does not eat meat or poultry — chicken is not allowed). Raw prawn salad: Suki is pregnant (five months along), and raw seafood is unsafe during pregnancy. Coconut ice cream with peanut brittle: this is for Mei's takeaway dessert, and Mei has a peanut allergy (anaphylactic reaction to peanut cookies) — peanut brittle is dangerous for her. Steamed sea bass with lime is fine: David eats fish now, it is cooked (safe for Suki), and has no peanuts. Pad thai with shrimp is fine for the table: although pad thai typically contains crushed peanuts, Mei will have already left by the time the main courses are served, so her peanut allergy does not apply to the table order. Mango sticky rice is fine as Mei's takeaway dessert: no peanuts or peanut-derived ingredients.
required_elements: Green curry chicken is problematic: David is pescatarian and cannot eat chicken (meat/poultry)
Raw prawn salad is problematic: Suki is pregnant and must avoid raw seafood
Coconut ice cream with peanut brittle is problematic for Mei's takeaway: peanut brittle violates Mei's peanut allergy
Steamed sea bass with lime is fine: David eats fish now, dish is cooked, no peanut ingredients
Mango sticky rice is fine for Mei's takeaway dessert: contains no peanuts
Pad thai with shrimp is acceptable for the table despite potentially containing peanuts, because Mei will have already left and her peanut allergy does not apply to the table order.
forbidden_elements: Flagging pad thai's peanuts as a problem for the table (Mei has already left, her peanut allergy does not apply to the table order)
Saying David cannot eat fish or seafood (he started eating fish again a month ago)
Saying David cannot eat the steamed sea bass (he eats fish now)
Treating Mei's peanut allergy as a general nut allergy (peanut allergy is specific to peanuts, coconut and tree nuts are not the same)
Flagging dishes as problematic for Mei's table dining (she is leaving early and only needs a takeaway dessert checked)
ground_truth.explanation: This scenario tests entity lifecycle tracking and inferential constraint reasoning across 9 conversational turns. The agent must track: (1) Mei has a peanut allergy inferred from her anaphylactic reaction to peanut cookies (throat swelling, ambulance), (2) David is vegetarian inferred from spending three years at an ashram in Rishikesh (ashram → vegetarian/sattvic diet), (3) David's constraint is NARROWED mid-conversation when he starts eating fish again (vegetarian → pescatarian — still no meat/poultry but fish is now OK), (4) Suki JOINS late with a pregnancy constraint inferred from being 'five months along' (pregnant → no raw or undercooked food), (5) Mei EXITS early with a scope change (leaving dinner but wants takeaway dessert → peanut allergy applies only to the takeaway dessert, not to the table order). At probe time, the active constraints are: David = pescatarian (no meat/poultry, fish OK), Suki = pregnant (no raw food), Mei = peanut allergy (takeaway dessert only). The key traps are: pad thai contains peanuts but Mei has left so it is fine for the table (removed entity trap); green curry chicken looks innocuous but David cannot eat chicken (constraint narrowing — he eats fish, not all animal products); and coconut ice cream with peanut brittle is specifically for Mei's takeaway where her allergy is active (scope distinction).

Steamed sea bass with lime is fine: David eats fish now, dish is cooked, no peanut ingredients
Mango sticky rice is fine for Mei's takeaway dessert: contains no peanuts
Pad thai with shrimp is acceptable for the table despite containing peanuts, because Mei will have already left

mechanism: Late-joiner with high-constraint: new person with strict needs arrives late
